If you are neurodivergent/disabled or have chronic illness, DO NOT book an appointment with Dr Rajput! I had an appointment with him recently and it was the most distressing experience I've ever had in a medical setting. From the outset of the consultation, I found Dr Rajput to be dismissive, continuously rude, and lacking in bedside manner, which immediately made both myself and my mother (who attended for support due to my autism and communication difficulties) feel unwelcome, unsafe and belittled. I had booked this appointment seeking help and guidance regarding my ongoing chronic health conditions.

One my main reasons for attending was to check/confirm whether one of my referrals that had been requested by my endocrinologist several weeks prior in a letter had been logged and sent. Despite acknowledging that this was something he was able to check for me, he refused to do so without providing a valid explanation, leaving me confused, unsupported and feeling disregarded. I also wished to briefly discuss some persistent symptoms I'd been experiencing as a result of my chronic illnesses and whether or not there could be any particular blood tests or further investigations into this.

I explained the symptoms I have been experiencing and asked if my routine blood tests could be arranged - something I have had many times previously as part of regular monitoring for my chronic illnesses. However, Dr Rajput appeared reluctant to authorise them with no reason given and made me feel as though I was being untruthful or burdensome, which was extremely distressing. I made every effort to explain my medical history so that he understood the importance of ongoing monitoring, yet I was repeatedly dismissed. His attitude throughout was belittling and disrespectful, adding further distress to an already vulnerable situation.

The interaction left me so overwhelmed that I began to cry, feeling helpless and unheard. Rather than responding with empathy or understanding, I was told to be quiet and lower my voice, despite speaking calmly and without raised volume. This felt highly inappropriate and unprofessional, especially considering my neurodivergence and visible distress.

As a direct result of how I was treated, I experienced an autistic meltdown in the hallway after leaving the consultation room. This was triggered by the emotional overload and lack of support shown during the appointment. Multiple staff members - nurses, doctors and reception staff - witnessed this incident. Eventually, I was assisted into a quiet room by staff (specifically Dr Jones who is an amazing doctor)  to help me recover. This was extremely exhausting, humiliating and distressing for both myself and my mother, and it should never have escalated to that point.

Since this incident, I have been left with severe anxiety about returning to the surgery building, as the experience was deeply traumatic for me. A place that should feel safe and supportive now feels intimidating and triggering, which is incredibly upsetting - especially considering I rely on your services for ongoing management of my chronic health conditions. This is not the outcome any patient should face after seeking medical care.

This experience has caused long-lasting emotional distress and has severely undermined my confidence in seeking medical support. I believe the treatment I received was far below acceptable NHS standards, particularly in regard to patient compassion, communication, and appropriate care for neurodivergent and disabled individuals.

I hope this comment is taken into account by anyone who reads it to protect other disabled, neurodivergent and chronically ill patients from receiving similar treatment.

Further to this, the VMC have handled the complaint I lodged about this matter very poorly which is incredibly disappointing as their patients should be at the core and heart of their actions.

I hope no other patient has to experience what I did. And I strongly advise that no other neurodivergent or disabled person ever have an appointment booked with him.",null,[0,240]]]],[],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sCi9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25rMVoyNUdlR3RJVmxOMU1sWnpXVlZ6VDFKMGJuYxAB!2m1!1s0x0:0x4a58b5f057ede342!3m1!1s2@1:CAIQACodChtycF9oOnk1Z25GeGtIVlN1MlZzWVVzT1J0bnc%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25rMVoyNUdlR3RJVmxOMU1sWnpXVlZ6VDFKMGJuYxAB&t=1&&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwiG4NyBz7GTAxWIToQGHbnpMccQoykIEygB"],null,[null,[[1,0]]]],"0ahUKEwiG4NyBz7GTAxWIToQGHbnpMccQ0pMFCBEoBQ"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFCaHBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEY3lSMVJaUzBwWmFsOWZSV2hEVm1aVVJVNDNSazkxZGpCa2MxTjJhMEZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVEpSYTBOYVRtZHZiR2xOV1VGRFNVRQ=="],[["Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tKV2RGRnZUR0paYkhSR1RHZE1aVFpxTFhkd1prRRAB",["0x0:0x4a58b5f057ede342",null,1765374614325045,1765374760087452,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/114244131201871539848/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Simon","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocLxuQ2njpLiVFjN_KaZ92tCKBPNLLOggCv6-jAqUo5tN3w1hw=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/114244131201871539848?hl=en"],"114244131201871539848",null,1,0,null,[0,2,1],0,["1 review",null,null,null,null,[null,"0ahUKEwiG4NyBz7GTAxWIToQGHbnpMccQ7LoGCBUoAA"]]]],null,"3 months ago",null,null,null,null,null,null,["Google","https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/product/1x/googleg_48dp.png",null,null,5],null,1],[[1],null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,["en"],[["I hope the nurse who was really rude to my friend today whilst trying to take her bloods is really pleased with herself for making my friend cry!
